## Changing a factor's range (Otava and Mylona, 2020, Figure 2)

If a follow-up experiment keeps `x3` within (-0.1, 0.1), interactions with
`x3` can contribute at most 0.1 × |δ| to the *other* factors' MPI. Main and
quadratic effects are unchanged, because MPI is a one-unit change on the coded
scale, and `x3`'s own MPI is unchanged because the other factors still span
their full ranges.

```{r}
b <- c(x1 = 0.4, x2 = 0.2, x3 = 0.2294, "x3^2" = 0.4185, "x2:x3" = 0.3706, "x1:x3" = 0.2)
base <- mpi(b, abs = TRUE)
mpi_adjust_range(base, list(x3 = c(-0.1, 0.1)))
```

Asymmetric ranges are handled exactly.

## Dropping factors (Otava and Mylona, 2020, Figure 4)

```{r}
mpi_subset(base, keep = c("x1", "x2"), others = "centre")
```

With `others = "centre"`, excluded factors are fixed at 0, so interactions
with them disappear. The two operations can be stacked in either order.
